note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a SOM 4; A06b SOM 4; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 7 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A01b (descent, born abroad: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from the father only, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.said: Person has been resident in Somalia for at least 7 years. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. ... n.a. (Note: nationality law provides that a person voluntarily acquiring another citizenship will lose Somali citizenship, while constitution provides that a person who is a Somali citizen cannot be deprived of Somali citizenship, even if s/he becomes a citizen of another country.) ... Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply) ... Person is born in Somalia to a father who is a citizen.; Person is born to a Somalia mother. Other conditions: see A06 (but residence period may be reduced to 2 years). ...
